key_insight: A learned linear convolution operator can parameterize atmospheric boundary layer turbulent fluxes more accurately and transparently than standard K-profile closures across stable and unstable regimes.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to improve coarse-resolution weather, climate, and engineering models by better representing momentum and heat exchange near the surface.
method: Train flux closures on high-resolution LES of idealized homogeneous-surface ABL flows across multiple stability regimes.
Represent nondimensional fluxes as a linearized convolution acting on nondimensional mean temperature and velocity profiles.
Select the best first-order closure by minimizing mean squared error on both training and unseen test cases, then verify stability in a posteriori single-column simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved predictive skill over a standard K-profile closure, and the learned model remains stable while closely matching LES in posteriori single-column tests.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on idealized homogeneous-surface LES cases, so generalization to complex terrain, heterogeneity, and real-world forcing needs further validation.
paper_title: Data-Driven Flux Parameterization for the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
